notes.meaning: Jesus warns his followers not to practice their religion just to show off for other people. Doing good deeds only to be praised ruins them in the sight of God. When people act for human applause, they lose any true blessing from their heavenly Father.

People should not announce their charity as if blowing a trumpet to draw a crowd. Hypocrites—actors playing a false role—give gifts publicly so everyone will think they are holy. Human praise is all the payment they will ever receive, with nothing left to receive from God.

Giving to the poor should be kept so quiet that even our own hands seem unaware of it. This means believers should not dwell on their good deeds or puff themselves up with pride. God notices what is done quietly and will gladly reward it.

Religious posers liked to stand in crowded public places at prayer times so everyone would notice their devotion. Jesus says prayer is meant for God, not for human audiences. Those who pray only to be admired already have their tiny prize in the applause of the crowd.

Personal prayer belongs in a private place where a person can shut out all distractions and focus entirely on God. God is present in quiet, hidden spaces and hears every humble cry. He marks these sincere, private moments and answers them graciously.

Pagans imagined that their gods would only respond if they chanted endlessly and repeated the same words over and over. True prayer does not depend on the length of a speech or fancy phrasing. God desires sincere requests from the heart rather than mindless, mechanical talking.

Believers do not pray to inform God of things he does not know or to wear him down. Our heavenly Father already understands all our needs before we speak. Prayer simply trains our hearts to trust him, lean on his care, and receive his good gifts.

Jesus provides a model pattern that shapes all Christian prayer. It begins by calling God our loving Father, giving believers confidence to approach him. We ask that his name—his holy character—be honored and treated with deep reverence by all people.

This request asks for God's loving rule to advance in human hearts and across the whole world. It also asks that people on earth may obey God as readily and completely as the holy angels do in heaven. Believers pray for the day when all rebellion against God ends.

After putting God's glory first, believers ask him for the physical food and daily supplies needed to sustain life. Asking only for today's bread keeps us depending on God step by step each day. It reminds us that even ordinary food is a merciful gift from our Creator.

Sins are described here as debts owed to God's justice because we have broken his laws and cannot repay him. We ask God to wipe away our guilt freely through his mercy. At the same time, we pledge that we are releasing the grudges and offenses others owe to us.

differ.view: Since believers are already declared righteous once for all through Christ, this daily prayer does not earn salvation but restores close fellowship with the Father after daily sins.
Forgiving others is a necessary condition and standard for receiving God's pardon, so holding on to grudges keeps God from forgiving our daily sins.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Justification is not a one-time legal verdict in the past but a continual cleansing, so an unforgiving person with a hardened heart cannot receive God's forgiveness.

notes.meaning: This petition expresses our deep weakness and asks God not to let us walk into dangerous trials that might overwhelm us. Believers pray to be protected from the snares of the devil and the power of sin. It seeks God's help to stand firm and escape the traps of evil.

Jesus emphasizes that people who expect God to pardon their own great sins must show mercy to others. Refusing to forgive injuries shows an unrepentant and hard heart that shuts itself off from God's mercy. A forgiving spirit proves that God's grace is truly at work inside us.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest these two verses were not originally spoken right after the prayer, but were placed here by the writer from another teaching of Jesus on forgiveness.

notes.meaning: Fasting is going without food for a time to humble oneself and focus on prayer. Hypocrites made themselves look miserable and covered their faces in ashes so everyone would admire their strict piety. Jesus warns that human admiration is the only reward such pretenders will ever receive.

When believers fast, they should wash and groom themselves as they would on any normal day. The goal is to keep private spiritual discipline hidden from human eyes so that only God is honored. The Father sees what is done quietly and will openly reward sincere devotion.

Earthly possessions, such as expensive clothes, stored crops, and money, easily rot, break down, or get stolen. Jesus urges his followers to invest in heavenly riches through acts of charity and faithful obedience to God. Heavenly treasures are completely safe and will never fade or be lost.

Whatever a person values most will naturally capture their attention, thoughts, and love. If our treasure is tied to earthly wealth, our lives will be pulled down into worldly worry. Setting our highest value on God draws our whole soul upward toward heaven.

The physical eye guides the movements of the body, and healthy vision keeps a person walking safely. In the same way, the inner eye represents a person's motives and spiritual focus. If our aim is single and fixed on God, our whole life stays bright and clear, but greedy and divided desires bring spiritual blindness.

A servant cannot belong completely to two owners whose commands conflict with each other. In the same way, a person cannot be fully devoted to God while also worshipping worldly wealth and gain. When wealth competes with God for first place in our heart, we must choose which one will rule us.

Jesus commands his followers to stop anxious worrying about their daily physical needs. God has already given us the greater gifts of life itself and our bodies. Since he created us, we can trust him to provide the lesser gifts of daily food and basic clothing.

Wild birds do not farm, harvest crops, or store grain in barns, yet God faithfully provides them with food each day. Human beings are created in God's image and are far more precious to him than birds. Since God cares for wild creatures, his own children can be certain he will not abandon them.

Anxious fretting is totally powerless to change our circumstances or lengthen our lifespan by even a short measure. God alone holds the days of our lives in his hands. Worrying only drains our energy and shows a lack of trust in his wise control.

Wild flowers grow without working or spinning cloth, yet God dresses them in breathtaking natural beauty. Even King Solomon, famous for his dazzling royal robes, could not match the lovely colors of a simple field lily. This shows how generously God decorates the natural world without human effort.

Common field grass lives only a brief time before withering away and being burned as fuel for clay baking ovens. If God lavishes such beauty on plants that quickly perish, he will surely provide clothes for his eternal children. Anxiety over basic needs reveals how weak our faith in his fatherly care can be.

Believers should not run around in panic over basic physical necessities. That kind of anxious scrambling belongs to people who do not know God or his loving care. Our heavenly Father already knows everything we need, and he can be trusted to take care of his family.

Our chief goal in life should be pursuing God's rule and living in holiness according to his will. When we put God's interests at the very top of our priorities, he promises to provide all our daily necessities as an extra blessing. Spiritual matters come first, and God takes care of the rest.

Jesus tells his disciples not to borrow future trouble by obsessing over what might happen tomorrow. Each day carries its own share of duties and difficulties, along with God's fresh mercies to handle them. We are meant to live one day at a time, trusting God for the strength we need today.
